{{Recipe summary
| Category = Meat recipes
| Servings = 2
}}

{{recipe}}

This is a classically-inspired steak recipe, with influences from both [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American]] and [[Cookbook:European cuisines|European cuisine]].

==Ingredients==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (16 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 550 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Beef#Loin|sirloin steaks]]
* [[cookbook:Montreal Steak Seasoning|Montreal steak seasoning]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] Cabernet Sauvignon [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Vinegar|balsamic vinegar]]
* 8–10 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], minced
* ⅓ large white [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], diced
* 4 cloves [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallots]], diced
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

==Procedure==
# Preheat a medium-sized [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over medium-low heat and preheat the [[Cookbook:Grill|grill]] to high.
# Add the onions to the pan, and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] until light yellow.
# Add the shallots and garlic to the pan and sauté for a few minutes more. Make sure all ingredients are lightly crisped.
# Pour in about ⅓ of the wine and ⅓ of the vinegar. Let this [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] and reduce over lower heat for about 5–10 minutes.
# Place the steaks on the [[Cookbook:Barbecue|barbecue]], seasoning with the Montreal steak spice.
# Add the rest of the wine and vinegar and season by sprinkling some fresh black pepper on top. Boil off until you no longer smell the alcohol coming from the steaming wine.
# Flip the steaks. You want them to be soft on the inside (cooked rare) yet quite charred on the outside, to get that charcoal flavor.
# Once the sauce has gone down to about ⅓ of its original volume, take off heat.
# Remove steaks from grill and take inside.
# Place the steaks on your plates, cover with the sauce and serve!

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You may wish to serve this flavourful dish with a side that compliments its strong flavors such as [[Cookbook:Asparagus|asparagus]], new [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], or roasted [[Cookbook:Brussels Sprout|Brussels sprouts]].
